items.title: 66960_Gil Evans oral history interview
items.q: The interviewee does not mention 'Smith' or any personal interaction with them; the mention is part of the interviewer's narrative about Jelly Roll Morton.

ctx.x: I've seen that happen a lot of times. I mean.......

I think Jelly Roll's car was repossessed or something and Smith was helping him out. Well anyway, it turned out that Jelly Roll went out to California with still New York licence plates on his car and he died while he was out there. And someone out there laid claim to the estate. And of course it was probated out there and people were totally unaware of what was going on.

So this man got, who owns so many rights to Jelly Roll's music is all tied up in litigation now trying to get something back from people who have absolutely no right to the estate at all. And they made out the will and left Jelly Roll's wife a dollar for instance. (LAUGHTER).
